title: A new cell wall has the least area that can enclose the given volume (Errera)

fields.label: Label
fields.value: A new cell wall has the least area that can enclose the given volume (Errera)

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: The fundamental rule of cell division is that the incipient partition of a dividing cell takes the least possible area that can divide the given volume; Sachs’s rule of successive divisions at right angles is a subordinate case of this principle.

fields.label: Notation
fields.value: partition \Sigma = \arg\min |\Sigma| subject to dividing V in the given ratio

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. VIII: The Forms of Tissues, or Cell-Aggregates (continued)

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: a much more important and fundamental rule, due not to Sachs but to Errera; that (3) the incipient partition-wall of a dividing cell tends to be such that its area is the least possible by which the given space-content can be enclosed.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter VIII, “The Forms of Tissues, or Cell-Aggregates (continued)”; topic “Sachs’s and Errera’s rules of division”. Scope: dividing cells, especially plant cells and blastomeres

fields.label: Notation
fields.value: partition \Sigma = \arg\min |\Sigma| subject to dividing V in the given ratio

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch08-02: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.81

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Modern computational geometry enables a direct observed-versus-optimal comparison in many archived divisions. The broad claim across plant cells and blastomeres and ambiguity about volume ratio prevent complete resolution from currently harmonized data.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Reconstruct each cell immediately before division, compute the least-area equal-volume partition under its boundary constraints, and compare it with the observed new wall.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Mechanical and developmental constraints may change the admissible minimum.

The phrase 'given space-content can be enclosed' is ambiguous for unequal divisions.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Errera's least-area rule is a direct comparison between an observed wall and a computable surface, and open embryo and meristem segmentations contain both the volumes and the walls. That comparison has already been framed on data of this kind and can be repeated or extended with current tools. Overlap with other geometric rules is a known bias and is reducible by choosing cells where the candidate surfaces differ.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: For symmetric divisions, compare the area of the observed partition with the least area that can divide the mother-cell volume, and with plausible larger alternatives such as a fixed genetic plane. Observed walls clustering on the area minimum would support Errera's rule; a systematic preference for a larger surface would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Computing a minimal surface is specialist but is an established method in this literature.

Several geometric rules nearly coincide in symmetric cells, so the test needs asymmetric and irregular mothers where the minimum is unique.

fields.label: Hypothesis
fields.value: In recently divided plant cells, the new wall between two sister cells has close to the least area of any planar cut that divides the reconstructed mother cell in the same volume ratio, and much less area than a cut of random orientation.

fields.label: Method
fields.value: analysis.py: for each wall flagged in *_new_walls.tif, the mother is the union of the two sisters; the observed interface area (anisotropic voxel faces) is compared with planar cuts at 500 Fibonacci-lattice orientations at the observed volume fraction. Per-division rows in derived/divisions.csv (regenerated by analysis.py, not committed); per-archive figures in derived/summary.json.

fields.label: Pass criterion
fields.value: Pre-registered. Data: the 8 alphabetically first meristem archives of Zenodo record 18711581 (Yates et al. 2026, Arabidopsis inflorescence shoot apices, 3D confocal, watershed-segmented). For each wall marked in *_new_walls.tif, the two cells it separates are sisters; the mother is their union (including the wall voxels between them). Both sisters must have volume >= 40 um^3 and must not touch the image border. Observed area A_obs = area of the voxel faces shared between the two sister regions in the mother mask (anisotropic voxel face areas from Metadata.txt). For 500 plane orientations spread uniformly over the hemisphere (Fibonacci lattice), the plane offset is set so the smaller side holds the observed smaller-sister volume fraction, and the cut area A(n) is measured with the same voxel-face rule. A_min = min over orientations; q = A_obs / A_min; percentile p = fraction of orientations with A(n) < A_obs. SUPPORTS if the median p over all divisions is <= 0.10 AND at least 50% of divisions have q <= 1.10.

fields.label: Fail criterion
fields.value: Pre-registered. REFUTES if the median p is >= 0.35 (observed walls are no smaller than typical random-orientation cuts) OR fewer than 20% of divisions have q <= 1.10. Any other outcome is MIXED. Fewer than 30 analysable divisions: inconclusive (underpowered).

fields.label: Unit
fields.value: median over divisions of the percentile of the observed new-wall area among 500 planar cuts of the mother at the observed volume ratio (voxel-face areas)

fields.label: Uncertainty
fields.value: 27249 divisions in 8 shoot apices; IQR of percentile 0.016-0.156

fields.label: Interpretation
fields.value: Errera's rule as Thompson states it: the incipient partition has the least area that can divide the given space-content. The 'given space-content' is the observed volume split of the two sisters, so asymmetric divisions are included. Real walls may be curved; the minimum is taken over planes, so a curved minimal wall can have q < 1, which still counts as consistent. Sisters are identified from the dataset's own detection of recently formed walls (its pipeline flags thin, recent walls), not from lineage tracking; mis-identified pairs work against the claim. Sachs's subordinate rule (right-angle alternation) is tested separately under thompson1917-ch08-01. The test is on one model plant tissue (Arabidopsis shoot apex), within the claim's scope 'dividing cells, especially plant cells'.

fields.label: Datasets
fields.value: Image processing data for manuscript: Control of plant organ growth through cell division orientation in inner tissues (Yates & Sablowski)

fields.label: Caveats
fields.value:
Mixed by the pre-registered thresholds: median percentile 0.062 passes (<= 0.10), but only 24.7% of divisions have q <= 1.10 (needs >= 50%; refutes below 20%). New walls are far smaller than random cuts (median 0.68 of the median random-cut area) but usually 10-40% above the least-area plane.

The q criterion is sensitive to how area is measured. The voxel-face rule inflates staircase surfaces that are oblique to the voxel grid. A sensitivity analysis that was not pre-registered (dividing face area by |n_x|+|n_y|+|n_z|) gives median q 1.04 and 65% within 1.10, which would pass. The pre-registered verdict stands.

Old walls (not flagged as new, analysed identically, not pre-registered) give median q 0.96 and 89% within 1.10. Either established walls relax towards least area after division, or the new-wall flags from the dataset pipeline pick thin, irregular walls that are measured less accurately.

Sisters are identified from the dataset flag for recently formed walls, not from lineage tracking; 3990 divisions touching the image border were excluded.

One tissue (Arabidopsis inflorescence shoot apex, 8 apices, 27,249 divisions); the minimum is taken over planes only.

Completed by the parent agent from the tester run output after the tester subagent stopped; the analysis ran unmodified.
